content.short: Grass pays people for the internet bandwidth they do not use, routing it into a network that gathers public web data for AI.
content.description: Grass users install a browser extension or app that shares their spare bandwidth. The network sends public web requests through these residential connections, which together form a large peer-to-peer scraping layer used to build AI training datasets. Contributors earn GRASS rewards in proportion to what they share, and the network is coordinated on Solana. Grass says more than 8.5 million people use it, and it runs quietly in the background on desktop, mobile or the Chrome extension, showing connection status and uptime on a dashboard.
content.meta: Share unused bandwidth to help collect public web data for AI and earn GRASS rewards. Explore Grass on Lancers Web3 Explorer.
